docs.title: MatCore
docs.text:
Material Core (MatCore) is a metadata standard for computational materials science. MatCore represents key aspects of a material-focused computation to make it understandable to the broad materials research community. It provides pragmatic and workable guidelines for documentation of materials data.

MatCore is developed as a grassroots effort by experts in first principles calculations, molecular dynamics, phase field, machine learning for materials, and related fields.

The MatCore effort is funded by the National Science Foundation, Division of Materials Research (DMR) through Award #2404283 and supported through the KIM Initiative.

docs.title: About MatCore
docs.text: The Material Core Metadata (MatCore) standard for computational materials science (CMS) represents key aspects of a material-focused computation to make it understandable to the broad materials research community. It provides pragmatic and workable guidelines for documentation of materials data.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
The primary goals of the MatCore standard are, by outlining expectations for metadata accompanying a computational dataset, to facilitate:

  • Dataset transparency, discoverability, sharing and reuse in theoretical and computational modeling.
  • Verification and validation of materials modeling and simulation software.
  • Training physics-based and machine learning models for material behavior.
  • Promote reproducibility in CMS by providing the information necessary for researchers to regenerate a published dataset.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The MatCore standard is focused on CMS methods aimed at computing material properties from a microscopic perspective, as opposed to computational methods in which the material is a component (such as engineering finite element analysis). The MatCore standard is designed to be flexible so that it can be extended to any area of CMS and can accommodate future changes in the field. An initial focus is placed on major CMS methods most widely used at the time of the creation of the standard with the aim of adding other methods in the future. The initial methods to be supported are:

  • Density functional theory
  • Many-body perturbation theory (GW, BSE)
  • Machine learning for materials
  • Molecular dynamics
  • Phase field
  • Derived approaches involving a combination of other methods

docs.title: Standard
docs.text: All methods share a common minimal set of metadata defined by the MatCore standard. The minimal MatCore metadata includes aspects of a dataset deemed important to report for data findability and reuse and are universal across all computational methods. In addition, each method has its own MatCore extension, e.g. MatCore-PS, MatCore-DFT, etc., that inherits from the minimal MatCore metadata and adds additional method-specific metadata.

docs.title: 1. Preamble
docs.text:
Material Core Metadata (MatCore) Standard

Version 0.6.0

docs.title: 1.1 Objectives
docs.text:
The Material Core Metadata (MatCore) standard for computational materials science (CMS) represents key aspects of a material-focused computation to make it understandable to the broad materials research community. It provides pragmatic and workable guidelines for documentation of materials data. Its goals are to make computational materials data FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable) and to contribute to its AI readiness.

The primary goals of the MatCore standard are, by outlining expectations for metadata accompanying a computational dataset, to facilitate: (1) dataset transparency, discoverability, sharing and reuse in theoretical and computational modeling, (2) verification and validation of materials modeling and simulation software, and (3) training physics-based and machine learning (ML) models for material behavior. An additional, more challenging, objective is to promote reproducibility in CMS by providing the information necessary for researchers to regenerate a published dataset.

docs.title: 1.2 Scope
docs.text:
The MatCore standard is focused on CMS methods aimed at computing material properties from a microscopic perspective, as opposed to computational methods in which the material is a component (such as engineering finite element analysis). The MatCore standard is designed to be flexible so that it can be extended to any area of CMS and can accommodate future changes in the field. An initial focus is placed on major CMS methods most widely used at the time of the creation of the standard with the aim of adding other methods in the future. The initial methods to be supported are:

  • DFT: Density functional theory

  • PIM: Particle interaction models

  • PS: Particle simulation (molecular dynamics, molecular statics, Monte Carlo and related methods)

  • MBPT: Many-body perturbation theory (GW/BSE)

  • ML: Machine learning

  • PF: Phase field

  • DER: Derived properties from CMS calculations

All methods share a common minimal set of metadata defined by the MatCore standard. In addition, each method has its own MatCore extension, e.g. MatCore-DFT, MatCore-PS, etc., that inherits from the minimal MatCore metadata and adds additional method-specific metadata.

Some methods supply energies and forces (e.g. DFT, or an interatomic potential), others use them to sample or evolve a system (e.g. MD). A dataset is described as one or more computations, each a group of calculations that share a method and its settings. A computation that uses the results of another names it, with the role the other plays: an ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) computation names the DFT computation that supplies its energies and forces. Each method-specific section describes the computations of its method. MatCore describes a dataset; it does not record how to reproduce its execution. The order of the calculations, their control flow and complete inputs belong to the provenance record of a workflow manager, to which a MatCore record may point.

docs.title: 1.3 Format
docs.text:
Each standard consists of a set of Properties with possible SubProperties, SubSubProperties, etc. The term “Property” will be used in the rest of this section to refer collectively to Property, SubProperty, etc. Properties have the following characteristics:

  • Each Property has a name consisting of a series of one or more words all in lower case separated by hyphens.

  • Required Properties are indicated by an asterisk (*) appended to the end of the Property name.

  • Properties have the following features:

    • Definition: A short explanation of the nature of the Property. Best-practice is to not use words from the Property name in the definition to prevent circular definitions, except in cases where confusion is unlikely.

    • Type: The data type of the Property's value: string, float, int, bool, file, or any (the instance states the type). A Property that only contains SubProperties has no type.

    • Extent: The shape of the value, in the notation of the Knowledgebase of Interatomic Models (KIM): [] for a scalar, [3,3] for a 3×3 array, [:] for a list of any length, or any when the schema does not fix it. A value with more than one dimension is a list of lists, the first index outermost: a value of extent [n,m] is a list of n entries, each a list of m components. A serialization preserves this nesting.

    • Values: The values the Property can take on, such as a controlled vocabulary, bounds, a format or a pattern, with examples.

      • When appropriate a controlled vocabulary can be defined. In this case sentence case format is adopted (i.e. for a phrase containing several words, the first letter of the first word is capitalized and all others are lower case except for proper names or acronyms). An option should always be added for users to add terms not included in the controlled vocabulary to allow the standard to support future developments. New terms may eventually be standardized and added to the controlled vocabulary.

      • When a controlled vocabulary is used, adoption of existing standards is recommended whenever possible.

      • A Property either has a value of its own or has SubProperties, never both. A physical quantity (a value whose Kind is neither "dimensionless" nor "inapplicable") is therefore a Property with two SubProperties, value and unit. In the Standard, value defines the Type, Extent, Kind and Recommended unit of the quantity. In a metadata instance, value holds the quantity and unit holds the unit in which it is expressed; unit SHALL be given, and SHALL be a symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U) whose Kind is compatible with the Kind of value. A property value without a unit, or with a unit incompatible with its Kind, is non-conformant; no default unit is ever implied. The Recommended unit listed for each property is informative and does not affect how values are interpreted. A pure number (a ratio, a fraction or a count) has the Kind dimensionless; it is a Property with a value of its own and carries no unit. Where a unit is given for a pure number, as in a generic parameter or a nondimensional length, it is the reserved symbol dimensionless. Plane angles use an angle unit (rad or degree). Where the meaning of a value depends on a convention that a unit cannot express (e.g. inclusion of a factor 2π in reciprocal lengths, or components given in a lattice basis), the property has a convention or basis subproperty, required as stated in its description. Some units (bohr, hartree, Ry) are defined through measured physical constants, so their values in SI units change slightly each time the Committee on Data of the International Science Council (CODATA) revises those constants; MatCore uses the CODATA 2022 values listed in Annex U.

      • A generic parameter holds a parameter whose meaning the Standard does not fix, such as a parameter of an exchange-correlation functional. It is a Property with four SubProperties, in this order: name (required), the designation of the parameter; value (required), whose Type, Extent and Kind are any, the metadata instance stating its type (float, int, string or bool) and its unit; unit (required), a symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), the reserved symbol dimensionless, or, if and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning); and description (optional), an explanation of the parameter.

      • A Property that contains SubProperties shows them nested within it.

    • Kind: The physical dimension of the Property's value, given as a MatCore Kind name (e.g. Energy, Length, InverseLength, Temperature, Pressure) mapped in Annex U to a QuantityKind Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI) of QUDT, an ontology of quantities, quantity kinds, units, dimensions and data types. Reserved values: dimensionless (ratios, counts), inapplicable (strings, identifiers, and the unit subproperty itself), any (a value whose Kind is given by the instance unit, as in a generic parameter).

    • Recommended unit: The unit customarily used for this Property in the community. Informative only; used by templates and tools.

    • Repeatable: A boolean variable that is “True” for Properties that may appear multiple times inside the metadata file. For example, for a dataset created by more than one person, the creator Property can be repeated as many times as needed, each with its own SubProperties.

    • Note(s): Additional clarifying information regarding a Property.

In addition to the required and optional Properties, other arbitrary Properties can be added to any MatCore Standard metadata files to support developments in the field. Such Properties may eventually be standardized and added to the MatCore Standard.

Examples are provided after each Standard specification in JSON, the first serialization adopted for MatCore instances. However, this is for clarification purposes only. The MatCore Standard serves as a conceptual and logical framework. It defines the schema for Properties required to ensure data consistency and interoperability. Critically, the MatCore Standard is implementation-agnostic. It dictates what information must be captured and how it should be structured logically, but it does not mandate a specific substrate, file format, or programming language.

A serialization is a file format (for example XML or JSON) together with the rules that map the MatCore data model onto it.

MatCore adopts Semantic Versioning (SemVer) three-part versioning system (major, minor, patch) to indicate Standard changes.

docs.title: 2.1 Minimal MatCore Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

The minimal MatCore metadata includes aspects of a dataset deemed important to report for data findability and reuse and are universal across all computational methods. The list of minimal metadata is tabulated below.

* required appears at most once repeatable

creator*

A primary entity (e.g. person, organization, software agent) responsible for creating the dataset's core content and their institutional affiliation if relevant.

Required Repeatable yes yes name*

The name of the entity that generated the dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Albert Einstein, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Claude Opus 5.5.

identifier

A unique, persistent identifier that globally and unambiguously identifies the entity that created the dataset.

Required Repeatable no yes value*

The identifier, in the form Annex I gives for its scheme when the scheme is listed there.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — scheme*

The identifier scheme that the value belongs to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: ORCID, ROR, DOI, SWHID, ISNI. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: For individuals, an ORCID ID; for organizations, an ROR ID; for software or AI agents, a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) generated specifically for the software code or version (e.g., a Zenodo software DOI) or a Software Heritage ID (SWHID) pointing to the exact software release or state. An ISNI may identify either individuals or organizations.

affiliation

The affiliation of the entity that generated the dataset if they have one.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The name of the affiliation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — identifier

A unique, persistent identifier that globally and unambiguously identifies the affiliation.

Required Repeatable no no value*

The identifier, in the form Annex I gives for its scheme when the scheme is listed there.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — scheme*

The identifier scheme that the value belongs to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: ROR, ISNI. Other values are allowed.

contributor

An entity (e.g. person, organization, software agent) that provided secondary support, specialized skills, or resources to the dataset's development, but is not considered a primary author, and their institutional affiliation if relevant.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The name of the entity that contributed to the dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Albert Einstein, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Claude Opus 5.5.

identifier

A unique, persistent identifier that globally and unambiguously identifies the entity that contributed to the dataset.

Required Repeatable no yes value*

The identifier, in the form Annex I gives for its scheme when the scheme is listed there.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — scheme*

The identifier scheme that the value belongs to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: ORCID, ROR, DOI, SWHID, ISNI. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: For individuals, an ORCID ID; for organizations, an ROR ID; for software or AI agents, a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) generated specifically for the software code or version (e.g., a Zenodo software DOI) or a Software Heritage ID (SWHID) pointing to the exact software release or state. An ISNI may identify either individuals or organizations.

affiliation

The affiliation of the entity that contributed to the dataset if they have one.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The name of the affiliation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — identifier

A unique, persistent identifier that globally and unambiguously identifies the affiliation.

Required Repeatable no no value*

The identifier, in the form Annex I gives for its scheme when the scheme is listed there.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — scheme*

The identifier scheme that the value belongs to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: ROR, ISNI. Other values are allowed.

title*

A single sentence description of the dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — creation-date*

The calendar date and time when the dataset was created.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: \d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])(T([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\dZ)?. Examples: 2021-02-22, 2021-02-22T14:30:00Z.

Clarifications: A date (YYYY-MM-DD), or a date and time in UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ), following the ISO 8601 Date and Time Format Standard.

description*

A synopsis of the dataset, its contents, and purpose.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: This can optionally include information on the format in which the dataset is stored (e.g. pointer to a relevant schema).

disclaimer

A statement of applicability provided by the creator(s) informing users of the intended use and/or limitations of this dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — structure*

A system modeled in the dataset, e.g. a bulk crystal or a thin film on a substrate, and the materials that make it up.

Required Repeatable yes yes label*

A name for this structure, by which computations in the record refer to it.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$. Examples: si-bulk.

Note: A label is unique among all labels of structures and computations in the record.

description

An explanation of the structure as a whole, e.g. the stacking order of its layers, the number of periods of a superlattice, or how its components meet.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — material-component*

One part of the structure, made of a single material, with its composition, form, role and phase.

Required Repeatable yes yes formula*

The chemical formula of the material component.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: [A-Za-z0-9.(){}+-]+. Examples: Si, SiO2, H2O2, Si0.7Ge0.3, Si{x}Ge{1-x}, (H2O)0.9(C2H6O)0.1, Ja0.8Jb0.2.

Clarifications: A formula is a sequence of terms. A term is an element symbol, a user-defined species or a group in parentheses, each followed by an optional count. An element symbol is one of the 118 symbols of the IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements (listed with atomic numbers 1 to 118 in the Standard Atomic Weights table of the IUPAC Commission on Isotopic Abundances and Atomic Weights). A user-defined species, for particles that are not chemical elements (e.g. in a Lennard-Jones model), is J followed by lowercase letters (e.g. Ja, Jlj); no element symbol begins with J. A count is a positive number, whole or decimal (e.g. H2O, Si0.7Ge0.3), or an expression in braces (e.g. Si{x}Ge{1-x}). A count of 1 is omitted. An expression contains at least one variable, given in variable, and is linear in its variables; it is built from numbers, one-letter variables, +, -, implied multiplication and parentheses (e.g. 1-x, 3x, 2(1-x)). A variable is used only when the composition varies, so a fixed composition is written with its numbers (e.g. Si0.3Ge0.7). A formula that is a sequence of two or more groups is a mixture of substances: the groups' counts are their mole fractions and sum to 1 (e.g. (H2O)0.9(C2H6O)0.1). Elements may appear in any order. A molecule is written with its molecular formula (e.g. H2O2, not HO). Separate phases, e.g. a film on a substrate, are separate material components.

variable

A value of a variable used in formula.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The name of the variable, as written in formula.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: [a-z]. Examples: x.

value*

A value of the variable.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] dimensionless — qualifier*

What the value represents.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Average, Final, Initial, Maximum, Minimum. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: The entries of one variable share its name, with at most one entry per qualifier.

topology

The structure of a substance in the material component, given by an identifier, when its formula alone does not determine it.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: Give topology only when the formula matches more than one isomer or polymorph and the data must say which, e.g. ethanol and dimethyl ether (C2H6O), or calcite and aragonite (CaCO3).

substance*

The formula of the substance, either a group in the material component's formula or the whole formula.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: C2H6O.

identifier*

An identifier of the substance's structure.

Required Repeatable yes yes value*

The identifier, in the form Annex I gives for its scheme when the scheme is listed there.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: InChI=1S/C2H6O/c1-2-3/h3H,2H2,1H3, CCO, ABC3_oP20_62_c_c_cd.

scheme*

The identifier scheme that the value belongs to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: AFLOW, InChI, SMILES. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: For a molecule, InChI is preferred where it can represent it; SMILES otherwise or in addition. For a crystal, the AFLOW prototype label.

form*

The geometric form of the component as modeled.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: 2D material, Bulk, Chain, Cluster, Molecule, Monolayer, Nanoparticle, Nanoribbon, Nanotube, Nanowire, Slab, Thin film. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: One of: "2D material" – A crystalline solid that is a single unit cell thick (typically a few nanometers or less), while extending infinitely or to large dimensions in the lateral plane, e.g. graphene. "Bulk" – A material extending without bound in all three directions, e.g. a periodic crystal or a liquid. "Chain" – A one-dimensional sequence of atoms or monomers, e.g. an isolated polymer chain or a monatomic chain. "Cluster" – A finite aggregate of atoms or molecules, smaller than a nanoparticle. "Molecule" – A single molecule. "Monolayer" – A single layer of atoms or molecules deposited on another material. "Nanoparticle" – A solid particle of nanometer size in all three directions. "Nanoribbon" – A strip of a 2D material of nanometer width. "Nanotube" – A hollow cylinder of nanometer diameter, e.g. a carbon nanotube. "Nanowire" – A solid wire of nanometer diameter, extending without bound along its axis. "Slab" – A truncated bulk structure that can be used, for example, to model surfaces. "Thin film" – A layer of finite thickness, free-standing or on a substrate. The form is that of the component as modeled, e.g. a substrate modeled as a slab is a Slab.

role

The part the component plays in the structure.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Adsorbate, Core, Film, Inclusion, Layer, Matrix, Shell, Solute, Solvent, Substrate. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: One of: "Adsorbate" – A molecule, cluster or particle on the surface of a substrate. "Core" – The inner part of a particle, enclosed by a shell. "Film" – A layer of finite thickness on a substrate. "Inclusion" – A material enclosed in a matrix, e.g. a precipitate or an embedded nanotube. "Layer" – One of the layers of a layered structure, e.g. a heterostructure, a superlattice or a stack of 2D materials. "Matrix" – A material that encloses one or more inclusions. "Shell" – A layer enclosing a core. "Solute" – A material dissolved in a solvent. "Solvent" – A liquid in which a solute is dissolved. "Substrate" – A material on which a film, layer or adsorbate lies. Give a role for each component when the structure has more than one.

fraction

The atomic fraction of the structure made up of this component, i.e. the number of atoms in the component divided by the number of atoms in the structure.

Required Repeatable no yes value*

The value of the property.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] dimensionless —

From 0 to 1.

Clarifications: The fractions of a structure's components sum to 1, for the entries without a qualifier and for each of Initial, Final and Average.

qualifier

What the value represents.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Average, Final, Initial, Maximum, Minimum. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: Without a qualifier, the value holds throughout the simulation and across the system, and the entry is the only one for the condition. Otherwise give one entry for each qualifier that applies, e.g. Initial and Final for a ramp, Minimum and Maximum for a range. For a vector or tensor, Minimum and Maximum are taken component by component.

phase

A phase of the material.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Amorphous, Single crystal, Polycrystal, Quasicrystal, Liquid, Gas, Plasma. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: One of: "Amorphous" – A solid material without crystalline order. "Single crystal" – A solid material characterized by a repeating pattern of atoms that extends throughout it without interruption. "Polycrystal" – A solid material made of more than one crystalline grain of differing orientation. "Quasicrystal" – A solid material with long-range order but without translational periodicity, e.g. one whose diffraction pattern shows five-fold rotational symmetry. "Liquid" – A fluid structure (e.g. the molten state of a material). "Gas" – A state where molecules or atoms are far apart and only interact during collisions. "Plasma" – A gas comprised of ions and electrons. Omit for a component whose form is Molecule.

magnetic-order

The arrangement of the magnetic moments in the material component as modeled.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Nonmagnetic, Ferromagnetic, Antiferromagnetic, Ferrimagnetic, Paramagnetic, Noncollinear. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Nonmagnetic" – No magnetic moments. "Ferromagnetic" – Moments aligned parallel. "Antiferromagnetic" – Equal moments aligned antiparallel, with no net moment. "Ferrimagnetic" – Unequal moments aligned antiparallel, with a net moment. "Paramagnetic" – Moments present but disordered, e.g. modeled as disordered local moments. "Noncollinear" – Moments not along one axis, e.g. a spin spiral.

description

An explanation of the nature of the material, e.g. a crystal structure designation, a chemical formula for a molecule, etc.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: e.g. a surface facet such as Pt(111), an orientation relationship such as (111)Pt ∥ (001)CeO₂, or the chirality of a nanotube.

microstructure

For a solid state phase, a description of the arrangement of phases, grains and defects in the material.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — computation*

A group of calculations in the dataset that share one method and one set of settings, e.g. the DFT single points of a training set.

Required Repeatable yes yes

Note: A simulation run in stages, e.g. heating, equilibration and a quench, is described as one computation for each stage whose method, settings or conditions differ and whose data the dataset contains or depends on. Each stage names the stage it continues from in input with the role Initial configuration, which carries over the final state of that stage, e.g. positions, velocities and the cell. These links give the order of the stages; the order of the entries in the record does not. A condition that changes within one stage, e.g. a temperature ramp, is given in that stage's conditions as entries with a qualifier. The full protocol, with its control flow and complete inputs, belongs to the provenance record of a workflow manager (§1.2).

label*

A name for this computation, by which other computations and the method-specific sections refer to it.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$. Examples: dft-single-points.

Note: A label is unique among all labels of structures and computations in the record.

method-class*

The general category to which the computational technique belongs.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Electronic, Atomistic, Mesoscopic, Continuum, Data-driven. Other values are allowed.

Note: The categories listed above are based on the MODA standard.

Note: For a PS computation, give the entity of its particles: Atomistic for atoms, Mesoscopic for coarse-grained particles such as beads.

method*

Examples: VASP.

role

The part this software played in the calculations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Calculation method, Interaction model, Script, Simulation code, Workflow framework. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: One of: "Calculation method" – A packaged procedure that computes a defined property, e.g. an OpenKIM test or an iprPy calculation. "Interaction model" – The implementation of a particle interaction model, e.g. a KIM model or a potential file; give its identifier and link. "Script" – Custom code written for the calculations, e.g. a Python script using ASE. "Simulation code" – A program that performs the simulation or calculation itself, e.g. LAMMPS or VASP. "Workflow framework" – A system that sets up, runs and manages calculations with other software, e.g. pyiron, AiiDA or MedeA.

description

What this software did in the calculations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — version

The version of the software package.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: 6.3.1.

Note: Give the version for an official release. For any other state of the code, e.g. a branch or a tag, give link and revision.

link

A URI for the software, e.g. its source repository or home page.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Format: uri (JSON Schema 2020-12).

revision

A tag or commit in the repository given in link.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Note: Give the full commit hash where possible; a tag or a branch can move.

identifier

A persistent identifier of the software or of the exact state of its code.

Required Repeatable no yes value*

The identifier, in the form Annex I gives for its scheme when the scheme is listed there.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — scheme*

The identifier scheme that the value belongs to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: DOI, SWHID. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: A Digital Object Identifier (DOI) for the software or a version of it (e.g. a Zenodo software DOI), or a Software Heritage ID (SWHID) for the exact state of its code, released or not.

dependency

A component the software was built with or ran on that can change its results.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: List the components that can change results, e.g. the compiler, the MPI, linear-algebra and FFT libraries, and libraries such as LibXC.

name*

The name of the component.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — version

The version of the component.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — role

The kind of component.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Compiler, FFT library, Interpreter, Library, Linear algebra library, MPI library. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: One of: "Compiler" – Translates source code into an executable, e.g. GCC or the Intel oneAPI compilers. "FFT library" – Computes fast Fourier transforms, e.g. FFTW. "Interpreter" – Runs a script, e.g. Python. "Library" – Any other library the software calls, e.g. LibXC or ASE. "Linear algebra library" – Provides BLAS, LAPACK or ScaLAPACK routines, e.g. OpenBLAS or Intel MKL. "MPI library" – Implements the Message Passing Interface (MPI), e.g. Open MPI or MPICH.

build-options

The options the software was built or run with that can change its results, e.g. compiler flags or enabled features.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — file

Input or output file for the software package associated with the computation. This includes the input file used to perform the computation, associated data files, and output generated by the software package. Most important are input files to enable reproduction of the dataset.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The file name.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — description*

A brief description of the file and its contents.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — contents

The contents of the file: its text, or its bytes encoded as given in encoding. Not required in case a link to the file is provided instead.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — encoding

How contents is encoded.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Base64. Other values are allowed.

Note: Without encoding, contents is the file's text. With Base64, contents is the file's bytes encoded as Base64 (RFC 4648); use it for a binary file, or for a text file whose exact bytes matter.

link

A URI pointing to a permanent location of the file online.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Format: uri (JSON Schema 2020-12).

checksum*

A digital fingerprint of the file, computed by a named algorithm.

Required Repeatable yes yes algorithm*

The algorithm that computed the checksum.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: SHA1, SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, BLAKE2b-256, BLAKE2b-384, BLAKE2b-512, BLAKE3, MD2, MD4, MD5, MD6, ADLER32. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: The algorithm names of SPDX 2.3.1 §8.4 (File checksum field).

value*

The checksum of the file, in lowercase hexadecimal digits.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: [0-9a-f]+.

publication

A publication that describes the dataset or the work that produced it, e.g. a journal article or preprint, to be cited when the dataset is used.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: The location where the dataset itself is stored is given in dataset-location.

reference*

Text that uniquely identifies the source of information being cited.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — doi

The digital object identifier (DOI) for the source.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: https://doi\.org/10\.[^/]+/.+. Examples: https://doi.org/10.1000/182.

link

A URI pointing to a permanent location of the source.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Format: uri (JSON Schema 2020-12). Examples: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.01568.

dataset-location

A repository where the dataset itself is stored and can be obtained.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: Omit when the metadata accompanies the dataset itself.

repository

The name of the repository.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Zenodo, Materials Cloud Archive.

doi

The digital object identifier (DOI) of the dataset in the repository.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: https://doi\.org/10\.[^/]+/.+. Examples: https://doi.org/10.17863/CAM.65004.

A URI pointing to the dataset in the repository.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Format: uri (JSON Schema 2020-12). Examples: https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/handle/1810/317974.

funding

Information about received monetary support or other resources to generate the dataset.

Required Repeatable no yes award-title

Name of the grant that provided funding to generate the dataset.

The funding agency that provided money and/or resources to generate the dataset.

The name of the funding agency.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: U.S. National Science Foundation.

A unique, persistent identifier that globally and unambiguously identifies the funding agency.

A funder identifier for the grant.

Another dataset that is connected to the current one in some manner.

Pointer to a related dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Format: uri (JSON Schema 2020-12).

description

Explanation of the relationship between the related content and the current dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — provenance

History of the dataset, detailing its origins and transformations.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: It is recommended to record the provenance of the dataset and to keep it current with each change.

event-type*

Description of change made to the dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Initial creation, Admin update, Version update, Metadata update. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Initial creation" – Initial creation of the dataset. "Admin update" – Editorial update to the dataset not requiring a version update (e.g. spelling correction). "Version update" – Change to the dataset or associated files requiring a new version. "Metadata update" – Change to the metadata, but not the dataset itself.

date*

The date and time when the change was made.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: \d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])(T([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\dZ)?. Examples: 2021-02-22, 2021-02-22T14:30:00Z.

Clarifications: A date (YYYY-MM-DD), or a date and time in UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ), following the ISO 8601 Date and Time Format Standard.

agent*

An entity (e.g. person, organization, software agent) responsible for the change, and their institutional affiliation if relevant.

The name of the entity that made the change.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

identifier

A unique, persistent identifier that globally and unambiguously identifies the entity that made the change.

Required Repeatable no yes value*

The identifier, in the form Annex I gives for its scheme when the scheme is listed there.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

The identifier scheme that the value belongs to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

comment

Explanation for the change in provenance.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — file

A file of the dataset, or associated with it, modified by the provenance event.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The name of the file.

A digital fingerprint of the file, computed by a named algorithm.

Clarifications: The algorithm names of SPDX 2.3.1 §8.4 (File checksum field).

value*

The checksum of the file, in lowercase hexadecimal digits.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: [0-9a-f]+.

matcore*

Information about this MatCore metadata record: the standard it follows, the dataset version it describes, and who created it and when.

Required Repeatable yes no standard-version*

The version of the MatCore standard this record follows.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: (0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*). Examples: 0.6.0.

standard-link

A URI for the schema of that version of the standard.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Format: uri (JSON Schema 2020-12).

Note: Give the DOI of the release where it has one; otherwise the address of the release's tag in the MatCore repository.

id*

An identifier of the dataset, the same for all its versions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: mc-ad83jsd3.

dataset-version*

The version of the dataset this record describes.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no int [] dimensionless —

Minimum: 1.

Note: The first version is 1. Each provenance event of type Version update starts a new version: the dataset's new version is described by a new record with the same id, its dataset-version raised by 1. Admin update and Metadata update events keep the version. When provenance is given, dataset-version is 1 more than the number of Version update events.

An entity (e.g. person, organization, software agent) responsible for creating this metadata record, and their institutional affiliation if relevant.

The name of the entity that created the metadata record.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

A unique, persistent identifier that globally and unambiguously identifies the entity that created the metadata record.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

An ISNI may identify either individuals or organizations.

affiliation

The affiliation of the entity that created the metadata record if they have one.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The name of the affiliation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — identifier

A unique, persistent identifier that globally and unambiguously identifies the affiliation.

Required Repeatable no no value*

The identifier, in the form Annex I gives for its scheme when the scheme is listed there.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — scheme*

The identifier scheme that the value belongs to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: ROR, ISNI. Other values are allowed.

creation-date*

The date, or date and time, when this metadata record was created.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: \d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])(T([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\dZ)?. Examples: 2021-02-22, 2021-02-22T14:30:00Z.

Clarifications: A date (YYYY-MM-DD), or a date and time in UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ), following the ISO 8601 Date and Time Format Standard.

license*

A contract defining the terms and conditions under which the dataset can be used.

Required Repeatable yes yes

Note: A license expression as defined in the SPDX specification, version 2.3.1, built from current identifiers of the SPDX License List: a single identifier (e.g. CC-BY-4.0) or a combination (e.g. CC-BY-4.0 OR CC0-1.0). Give the SPDX short identifier, not the license's full name, so that the value can be read by tools. A license not on the SPDX License List, including a custom license, is written LicenseRef- followed by letters, digits, - or . (e.g. LicenseRef-NIST-data), with its name and a link to its full text, both required in this case. A license for data is usually one written for data, e.g. CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0 or ODbL-1.0, rather than one written for software.

docs.title: 2.2 Density Functional Theory (DFT) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

The metadata for density functional theory (DFT) data (MatCore-DFT) is tabulated below. This includes the level of theory (exchange-correlation functional, core-electron treatment and wavefunction representation) and associated parameters. The properties are given in settings blocks, each naming the DFT computations it describes. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

settings*

Settings shared by the computations named in it.

Required Repeatable yes yes computation-label*

The label of a computation these settings apply to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable — xc-functional*

Approximation used to describe the electron exchange and electron correlation energies

Required Repeatable yes yes type*

The mathematical form of the exchange-correlation functional.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: LDA, GGA, Meta GGA, Hybrid, ML. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "LDA" – Local Density Approximation. "GGA" – Generalized Gradient Approximation. "Meta GGA" – Extension to GGA including dependence on Laplacian of electron density. "Hybrid" – An approximation for the exchange-correlation (XC) functional that includes a portion of the exact XC from Hartree–Fock theory or machine learning with the rest coming from other sources (ab initio or empirical). "ML" – Machine learning based functional.

name

The exchange-correlation functional as the author names it.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: Examples of possible content by type: LDA: Common parameterizations: VWN, PW92, etc. GGA: Typical choices are PW91, PBE, rPBE, revPBE, BLYP, etc. Meta GGA: Specific named examples include TPSS, SCAN, M06, etc. Hybrid: B3LYP, PBE0, HSE03, HSE06, NeuralXC, DeePKS, … ML: DM21, NNLDA, NNGGA, CIDER, etc. Others: BEEF, etc. A decomposition into the components of a community library such as LibXC is given in normalization. Give the functional alone, without a dispersion correction (e.g. PBE, not PBE-D3); the correction is given in dispersion-correction.

description

Explanatory text providing more information about the type of the exchange-correlation method used including any relevant identifying information.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: Free text on what type and name do not say, e.g. a modification of the functional or the reason for choosing it.

normalization

The functional decomposed into the components of a community library, which names the components.

Required Repeatable no no components*

The components of the functional, in the identifiers of the source.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [:] inapplicable —

Examples: [GGA_X_PBE, GGA_C_PBE].

source*

The library whose identifiers the components use.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: LibXC. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "LibXC" – the Libxc library of exchange-correlation functionals.

Note: Give the version of the library as a dependency of the simulation code in minimal software.

xc-parameter

A fixed variable associated with the specified exchange-correlation functional method.

Required Repeatable no yes

Note: For example, the mixing parameter of a hybrid exchange-correlation functional, or another method-specific parameter.

name*

The designation of the exchange-correlation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the exchange-correlation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit*

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — core-electron-treatment*

The treatment of the core electrons in the calculation.

Required Repeatable yes no type*

The method used to treat the core electrons.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: All-electron, PAW, Pseudopotential. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "All-electron" – All of the electrons in an atom are modeled explicitly. "PAW" – Projector Augmented Wave. "Pseudopotential" – Valence electrons are treated explicitly, and core electrons are modeled by a simplified potential.

pseudopotential-or-paw

For type "Pseudopotential", or type "PAW", additional information about each pseudopotential or PAW dataset.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The name of the pseudopotential or PAW dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — species*

The element or user-defined species this pseudopotential or PAW dataset is for, as written in a material component's formula.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Si, Ja.

type*

The physical form of the pseudopotential or PAW dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Norm conserving, PAW, Ultrasoft. Other values are allowed.

description

Explanatory text about the pseudopotential or PAW dataset including any relevant identifying information.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — number-of-valence-electrons*

The number of electrons treated explicitly.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no int [] dimensionless —

Minimum: 1.

repository

The database from which the pseudopotential or PAW dataset was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — version

The version of the pseudopotential or PAW dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: 6.3.1.

doi

The digital object identifier (DOI) for the pseudopotential or PAW dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: https://doi\.org/10\.[^/]+/.+.

file

The pseudopotential or PAW dataset file, with its checksums.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Use file when the pseudopotential or PAW dataset is identified by a checksum of its file (e.g. the SHA256 hash of a VASP POTCAR file). For any other designation, use unique-identifier.

name*

The name of the file.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — checksum*

A digital fingerprint of the file, computed by a named algorithm.

Required Repeatable yes yes algorithm*

The algorithm that computed the checksum.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: SHA1, SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, BLAKE2b-256, BLAKE2b-384, BLAKE2b-512, BLAKE3, MD2, MD4, MD5, MD6, ADLER32. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: The algorithm names of SPDX 2.3.1 §8.4 (File checksum field).

value*

The checksum of the file, in lowercase hexadecimal digits.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: [0-9a-f]+.

unique-identifier

A token other than a checksum that identifies the pseudopotential or PAW dataset, such as a label or code assigned by the library that distributes it.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Note: For a checksum of the pseudopotential or PAW dataset file, use file instead.

wavefunction-representation*

The representation used to expand the electronic wave functions.

Required Repeatable yes no type*

The method used to represent the electronic wave functions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Gaussian basis sets, LAPW, Local atomic orbitals, Numerical atomic orbitals, Plane waves, Real space grids. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: The terms fall into three groups. (1) Basis-function expansions: "Gaussian basis sets" – Atom-centered Gaussian-type orbitals. "Local atomic orbitals" – Atom-centered orbitals of a form not covered by the previous or the next term, e.g. Slater-type orbitals. "Numerical atomic orbitals" – Atom-centered orbitals tabulated numerically, zero beyond a cutoff radius. "Plane waves" – Periodic plane waves up to a kinetic-energy cutoff. (2) Grid methods: "Real space grids" – Values on a mesh of points in real space (finite differences or finite elements). (3) Augmented methods: "LAPW" – Linearized Augmented Plane Wave: atomic-like functions inside spheres around the atoms, plane waves between them.

localized-orbital-basis-set

For type "Gaussian basis sets", "Local atomic orbitals" or "Numerical atomic orbitals", additional information about the basis set.

Required Repeatable no yes type*

The designation of the set of orbital functions used for expanding electronic wave functions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: 6-31G, DZP.

species

The element or user-defined species this basis set is for, as written in a material component's formula.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Note: Give the species this basis set is used for. Omit it when one basis set is used for every species.

repository

The database from which the localized-orbital basis set was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — version

The version of the localized-orbital basis set.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — doi

The digital object identifier (DOI) for the localized-orbital basis set.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: https://doi\.org/10\.[^/]+/.+.

file

The localized-orbital basis set file, with its checksums.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Use file when the basis set is identified by a checksum of its file. For any other designation, use unique-identifier.

name*

The name of the file.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — checksum*

A digital fingerprint of the file, computed by a named algorithm.

Required Repeatable yes yes algorithm*

The algorithm that computed the checksum.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: SHA1, SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, BLAKE2b-256, BLAKE2b-384, BLAKE2b-512, BLAKE3, MD2, MD4, MD5, MD6, ADLER32. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: The algorithm names of SPDX 2.3.1 §8.4 (File checksum field).

value*

The checksum of the file, in lowercase hexadecimal digits.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Pattern: [0-9a-f]+.

unique-identifier

A token other than a checksum that identifies the localized-orbital basis set, such as a label or code assigned by the library that distributes it.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Note: For a checksum of the basis set file, use file instead.

kinetic-energy-cutoff

For type "Plane waves", or for "LAPW" when the code takes the cutoff as an energy, the maximum kinetic energy of the plane waves included in the calculation of wave functions.

Required Repeatable no no value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Energy eV

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — lapw-basis-cutoff

For type "LAPW", the cutoff of the basis, given as the product of the smallest muffin-tin radius and the largest plane-wave wavevector, RMTKmax (RKmax).

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no float [] dimensionless —

Minimum: 0.

charge-density-cutoff

For type "LAPW" or "Plane waves", the energy value used to truncate the plane wave expansion of the electron charge density.

Required Repeatable no no value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Energy eV

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — calculation-physics

Additional phenomena included beyond the standard DFT calculation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Collinear spin polarization, Noncollinear spin polarization, On-site correlation, Orbital polarization, Spin-orbit coupling, Van der Waals. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Collinear spin polarization" – Spin-polarized, with all magnetic moments parallel or antiparallel to one axis. "Noncollinear spin polarization" – Spin-polarized, with magnetic moments free to point in any direction. "On-site correlation" – e.g. DFT+U. "Orbital polarization" – A correction that enhances the orbital magnetic moment, e.g. Brooks' orbital-polarization term. "Spin-orbit coupling" – The coupling of the electron spin to its orbital motion. "Van der Waals" – Dispersion interactions, by a correction or a nonlocal functional. Give at most one of the two spin-polarization terms. List each phenomenon as a separate entry, e.g. a noncollinear calculation with spin-orbit coupling has two entries, "Noncollinear spin polarization" and "Spin-orbit coupling".

initial-magnetic-moment

The magnetic moment per atom of a species at the start of the self-consistent cycle.

Required Repeatable no yes species*

The element or user-defined species whose atoms start with this moment, as written in a material component's formula.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float any MagneticMoment mu_B

Note: A signed number for collinear spin polarization; a vector of three Cartesian components for noncollinear spin polarization, as calculation-physics states.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — dispersion-correction

The additive correction for van der Waals dispersion applied to the functional.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: D2, D3, D3(BJ), D4, TS, MBD. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "D2", "D3", "D4" – Grimme's corrections of those generations. "D3(BJ)" – D3 with Becke–Johnson damping. "TS" – Tkatchenko–Scheffler. "MBD" – Many-body dispersion.

Note: Give it when calculation-physics lists Van der Waals and the dispersion is added to the functional. A functional that includes dispersion itself (e.g. vdW-DF, rVV10) is named in xc-functional › name.

k-point-mesh

For periodic systems, a grid of points sampled within the Brillouin zone, used to approximate integrals and calculate electronic properties by discretizing the wavefunction across reciprocal space.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: The mesh samples the Brillouin zone of the simulation cell (minimal conditions › cell), periodic in the directions given by cell-periodicity. When the mesh differs between the configurations of a computation, e.g. one chosen from a k-point spacing, omit number-of-points and say in comment how the mesh was chosen.

type*

The choice of how k-points are distributed on the mesh.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Regular gamma-centered, Regular shifted, Irregular. Other values are allowed.

number-of-points

The number of k-points included along each reciprocal lattice vector.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no int [3] dimensionless —

Minimum: 1, for each component.

Clarifications: Ordered list of three integers, the number of k-points along the three reciprocal lattice vector directions.

shift

Translation of the k-point mesh along the reciprocal lattice vector directions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no float [3] dimensionless —

Clarifications: Ordered list of three real numbers, the shifts along the three reciprocal lattice vector directions. Shifts are given as fractions of the mesh spacing along each reciprocal lattice vector.

smearing

The method of assigning fractional occupations to electronic states near the Fermi level, and its parameters.

Required Repeatable no no type

The choice of method for assigning fractional occupancies of electronic states and/or facilitating reciprocal space integrations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: None, None - tetrahedron, None - Blöchl-corrected tetrahedron, Gaussian, Fermi-Dirac, Methfessel-Paxton, Marzari-Vanderbilt. Other values are allowed.

width

A parameter that controls the broadening of the electron energy levels near the Fermi level.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Give the width as an energy; for Fermi-Dirac smearing it is kBT, where T is the electronic temperature. It is not a temperature imposed on the simulated system, which is given in conditions.

value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Energy eV

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — parameter

A fixed variable associated with the specified smearing method (e.g. the order of the Methfessel-Paxton method).

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The designation of the smearing parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — value*

The data associated with the smearing parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no any any any — unit*

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable — self-consistent-field-convergence

Method and termination criteria defining the precision of self-consistent solution of the Kohn-Sham equations.

Required Repeatable no no method-density

The self-consistent field mixing and/or extrapolation scheme for the iterative solution of the Kohn-Sham equations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Simple mixing, Pulay mixing, DIIS, Broyden mixing. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "DIIS" – Direct Inversion in the Iterative Subspace.

method-diagonalization

The method used to obtain the Kohn-Sham orbitals at each step of the self-consistent loop.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Car-Parrinello, Chebyshev filtering, Conjugate gradient, Davidson method, Direct diagonalization, Lanczos, LOBPCG, RMM-DIIS. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Car-Parrinello" – Fictitious dynamics of the electronic orbitals, which replaces diagonalization. "Chebyshev filtering" – Subspace iteration with Chebyshev polynomial filters. "Davidson method" – Including blocked variants. "Direct diagonalization" – A dense eigensolver applied to the full Hamiltonian matrix (e.g. LAPACK, ScaLAPACK). "LOBPCG" – Locally Optimal Block Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient. "RMM-DIIS" – Residual Minimization Method with Direct Inversion in the Iterative Subspace.

tolerance*

Convergence criterion for the self-consistent loop.

Required Repeatable yes no criterion*

The quantity whose convergence the tolerance measures.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Energy, Charge density, Potential. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Energy" – The change in the energy between successive iterations, defined as for relaxation-tolerance-energy. "Charge density" – The change or residual of the electron density. "Potential" – The change or residual of the Kohn-Sham potential.

value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] any —

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit in which the associated value is expressed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Clarifications: A symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U), or the reserved symbol dimensionless. If and only if no Annex U symbol applies, a string prefixed x-gnu: giving a GNU Units expression (accepted with a validation warning).

relaxation-tolerance-energy

Energy convergence criterion for atomic relaxation.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: The energy is the Helmholtz free energy F = E − TS, including the entropy S of the smeared electrons at the smearing temperature T, when occupations are smeared (e.g. a metal), and the total energy E otherwise (e.g. an insulator). It is not the energy extrapolated to zero smearing.

Note: Give it when the computation's task is Optimization.

value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Energy eV

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — relaxation-tolerance-forces

Maximum force convergence criterion for atomic relaxation.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Give it when the computation's task is Optimization.

value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Force eV/angstrom

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — relaxation-tolerance-stress

Maximum stress convergence criterion for cell relaxation, relative to the stress imposed in conditions.

Required Repeatable no no

Note: Give it when the computation's task is Optimization.

value*

The value of the property, in the unit given by unit.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no float [] Pressure GPa

Minimum: 0.

unit*

The unit of the value, an Annex U symbol whose Kind is the Kind of value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable — comment

Additional information on the DFT calculation. For example, non-self-consistent constraints, such as details about imposed state occupation or moment freezing.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes string [] inapplicable —

docs.title: 2.5 Many-Body Perturbation Theory (MBPT) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

The metadata for Many-Body Perturbation Theory (MBPT) data (MatCore-MBPT) is tabulated below. This includes the MBPT method, starting point, dielectric treatment, and associated parameters. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard and MatCore-DFT standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

mbpt-method*

The many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) approach used and associated settings.

Required Repeatable yes no type*

The nature of the MBPT calculation performed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "GW" "BSE" "GW/BSE" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

self-consistency*

Specifies the level of iterative updating applied to the Green's function (G), the screened Coulomb interaction (W), or the excitonic Hamiltonian during the calculation. This property identifies whether the MBPT equations are solved in a 'one-shot' perturbative manner or through an iterative cycle where the electronic or excitonic quasiparticle states are updated to reach a self-consistent solution.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values depending on the variant of the GW, BSE, or GW/BSE approach used: "G0W0" – One-shot calculation; the G and *W *are constructed using the starting eigenvalues and wavefunctions. "GW0" – Only the Green's function G is updated iteratively, while *W *remains fixed at the *W0 *level "G0W" – Only the screened interaction W is updated iteratively, while G remains fixed at G0 "scGW" – Fully self-consistent GW; bothG* and W are updated iteratively until the quasiparticle energies and/or wavefunctions converge "QSGW" – Quasiparticle self-consistent GW; the starting potential is updated to provide the optimal independent particle basis for the GW expansion "BSE0" – One-shot BSE; the excitonic Hamiltonian is built once using fixed GW quasiparticle energies and screening (W) "scBSE" – Self-consistent BSE; internal refinement of the kernel or energies within the BSE process "evGW+BSE" – Eigenvalue-only self-consistent GW (evGW) used as the starting point for a subsequent BSE calculation "scGW+BSE" – The BSE is solved using the results of a fully self-consistent GW calculation Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

starting-point*

The density functional theory (DFT) exchange-correlation functional used to generate Kohn-Sham wavefunctions and eigenvalues for the Green's function and the screened Coulomb interaction.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "LDA" "GGA" "Meta GGA" "Hybrid GGA" "DFT+U" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

dielectric-matrix*

Information on the dielectric matrix used to compute the screened Coulomb interaction W.

Required Repeatable yes no planewave-basis-cutoff

For a planewave code, the basis set cutoff employed for the dielectric matrix. This is the same as the kinetic energy cutoff.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A real number containing the cutoff.

Legacy unit: Rydberg (Ry)

Note: Specify either "planewave-basis-cutoff" or "localized-orbital-basis-set", but not both.

localized-orbital-basis-set

For local orbital codes, the name of the basis set .

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the name of the atomic orbital basis. (e.g. "cc-pV6Z").

Note: Specify either "planewave-basis-cutoff" or "localized-orbital-basis-set", but not both.

frequency

The method used to handle the frequency dependence of the Green's function, the screened Coulomb interaction, and their product.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Hybertsen-Louie" "Godby-Needs" "Full frequency real axis" "Full frequency imaginary axis" "Contour deformation" "Spacetime" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

response-basis-size

For sum-over-states methods, the number of bands used in the sum. For linear-response methods, the number of dielectric eigenvalues.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer containing the number of bands or eigenvalues.

Legacy unit: dimensionless

q-points*

Brillouin zone grid used for sampling the dielectric matrix.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: Ordered list of 3 integer numbers containing the number points along the three reciprocal lattice vector directions.

Legacy unit: dimensionless

coulomb-truncation

Method used to eliminate long-range Coulomb interactions between periodic replicas in supercell calculations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Ismail-Beigi" "Rozzi" "Spencer-Alavi" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

gw-bands

Number of bands for which the GW correction is evaluated.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer specifying how many bands are corrected, counting from the bottom of the valence bands.

Legacy unit: dimensionless

bse-hamiltonian

A collective descriptor for the parameters defining the construction, dimensionality, and solution method of the effective excitonic Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian that is being solved in a BSE calculation. It characterizes the Hilbert space size and the physical constraints (momentum and spin) applied during the diagonalization

Required Repeatable no no number-valence-bands

Number of valence bands included in the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer specifying how many valence bands are corrected, counting from the valence band top.

Legacy unit: dimensionless

number-conduction-bands

Number of conduction bands included in the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer specifying how many bands are corrected, counting from the conduction band bottom.

Legacy unit: dimensionless

k-point-mesh

Brillouin zone grid used for building the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Ordered list of 3 integer numbers containing the number points along the reciprocal lattice vector directions.

Legacy unit: dimensionless

exciton-momentum

Crystal momentum of the exciton in the BSE calculation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: Ordered list of 3 real values containing the crystal momentum in fractions of the reciprocal lattice vectors (dimensionless), e.g. [0.5,0.5,1.0].

Legacy unit: dimensionless

exciton-multiplicity

Specification whether the BSE calculation is performed for singlet or triplet excitons.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: string containing one of the values: "Singlet" "Triplet" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

diagonalization

Approximation method used to diagonalize the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Tamm-Dancoff" "Full diagonalization" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

number-lowest-eigenvalues

Number of lowest eigenvalues computed by solving the BSE Hamiltonian.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: One integer containing the number of BSE eigenvalues.

Legacy unit: dimensionless

bse-kernel-truncation

Method used to eliminate long-range Coulomb interactions between periodic replicas in the BSE Coulomb kernel.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Ismail-Beigi" "Rozzi" "Spencer-Alavi" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.
