docs.title: 2.6 Machine Learning (ML) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

The metadata for Machine Learning (ML) data (MatCore-ML) is tabulated below. This metadata documents key aspects of the ML method to provide understanding of the dataset generated by it. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

ml-task*

Characterization of the machine learning process performed.

Required Repeatable yes yes type*

The nature of the machine learning task.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Property prediction" "Structure prediction" (e.g. crystal structure prediction) "Structure generation" (e.g. de novo crystal generation) "Synthesis prediction" "Material ranking" "Clustering" "Embedding" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

Note: This Property can be repeated if the machine learning task involves multiple types of calculations.

description

Explanation of the machine learning task performed.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a more detailed explanation of the machine learning task and its objectives.

ml-model*

A comprehensive description of the machine learning approach and architecture used.

Required Repeatable yes no algorithm*

The machine learning method used.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of the machine learning algorithm used (e.g. neural network, random forest, Gaussian process, etc.)

target-variable*

The desired output or answer the machine learning model aims to predict.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of a target variable the machine learning model aims to predict.

input-feature

Information provided to the machine learning method.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of the form and meaning of an input variable/feature provided to the machine learning model (e.g. a graph representation of a crystal structure). This can include information on feature engineering performed to define the input (e.g. dimensionality reduction, clustering, etc.).

model-architecture

A description of the network topology used by the specified algorithm.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of the model architecture used by the specified algorithm (e.g. for a neural network: the number of layers, nodes per layer, etc.).

model-size

A measure of the magnitude of the machine learning architecture.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of the size of the trained model (e.g. number of parameters, storage space, memory requirements, etc.)

training-data

The information used for parameterizing the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

Name of the training dataset used to train in the machine learning model.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing the dataset name.

contents*

Description of the information included in the training dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing a description of the training data (e.g. DFT calculations, experiments, etc.)

source

Location from which the training data was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a MatCore ID, web address, DOI, citation, or other description of the source of the training data.

size

Number of items in the training dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing information on the number of data points, configurations, etc., in the training set.

data-preprocessing

Approach used for preliminary refining of raw, unformatted, or incomplete information into a structured and clean state suitable for modeling or analysis.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing a description of any preprocessing applied to the dataset to prepare it for training the machine learning model.

missing-data

Documentation of incomplete, null, or unrecorded entries within a feature set that hinder algorithm training.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A description of missing entries in the raw dataset (e.g. percentage of missing data and explanation of which fields are missing and why).

missing-data-strategy

Approach used for filling in or removing blank, null, or unknown entries in a dataset.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string describing the approach used for handling missing data.

outlier-handling

Approach to identifying and addressing extreme observations that deviate significantly from the general distribution to ensure they do not disproportionately skew model training.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the method used to detect and handle outliers.

dataset-split

A description of how information used to train the machine learning model was divided into subsets as part of the training process.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

docs.title: 2.7 Phase Field (PF) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

The metadata for Phase Field (PF) data (MatCore-PF) is tabulated below. This metadata documents key aspects of the PF method to provide understanding of the dataset generated by it. This includes the fundamental mathematical and physical framework governing the PF simulation, including the governing equations, thermodynamic free energy models, and time-evolution state. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

physical-phenomena*

Material process being modeled; description of the overarching processes and mechanisms being modeled/simulated.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Isothermal solidification" "Directional solidification" "Isothermal annealing" "Sintering" "Twinning" "Grain growth" "Spinodal decomposition" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

problem-specification*

The fundamental mathematical and physical framework governing the phase field simulation, including the governing equations, thermodynamic free energy models, and time-evolution state

Required Repeatable yes no time-dependence*

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "Property prediction" "Transient evolution" "Steady state" "Stationary" "Thermodynamic equilibrium" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

governing-equation*

The specific phase field equation used to evolve a field variable.

Required Repeatable yes yes type*

The mathematical classification of the phase field equation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "CH" – Cahn-Hilliard "AC" – Allen-Cahn "GP" – Grand Potential "FID" – Finite Interface Dissipation "PFC" – Phase Field Crystal "Fluid" "Multi" "Coupled" "Diffuse" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

evolved-variable*

The name of the field-variable that this equation solves for.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

driving-energy

A free energy component that acts as a forcing term in this equation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes — — — —

free-energy*

The thermodynamic free energy function used in the system

Required Repeatable yes no name*

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "1D" "2D" "3D" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

A description of the computational framework used to solve the phase field equations.

Required Repeatable yes yes spatial-discretization*

Legacy unit: dimensionless

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the units of the value in the GNU unit convention (or the text "dimensionless").

description

An explanation providing further clarification on the grid spacing parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string explaining the grid spacing parameter.

time-step-size

The discrete duration of progression between consecutive stages of a simulation, determining the interval for numerical integration, resolution of transient phenomena, and stability of the governing equations.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The designation of the time step size parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the name of the time step metric, (e.g., "dt", "initial", "min", "max").

value*

The data associated with the time step size parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

unit*

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the units of the value in the GNU unit convention (or the text "dimensionless").

description

An explanation providing further clarification on the time step size parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string explaining the time step size parameter.

solver

Specific numerical algorithm or backend used for solving the equations.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no yes — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the solver name (e.g., "Newton-Krylov", "GMRES").

Explicit data structure capturing changing and unchanging elements of the physics model.

Required Repeatable no no model-parameter

A specific, adjustable, or calibrated numeric value that controls certain aspects of the simulation.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The designation of the model parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

The data associated with the model parameter.

docs.title: 2.8 Derived Property Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

The metadata for derived properties (MatCore-Der) is tabulated below. This refers to properties computed from data generated using a CMS method documented elsewhere in this section (e.g. spectroscopy computations based on DFT data). (Notes: (1) This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard and one of the associated methods metadata, adding the properties below. (2) Derived properties in this category are limited to properties based on a single method. Derived properties involving a combination of multiple methods (e.g. MD and ML) are not supported. An exception is MBPT, which itself is based on DFT.)

Examples of derived properties include:

  • Electronic (band structure, density of states (DOS), projected DOS, dielectric function, charge and bonding analysis, etc.)
  • Electron-phonon interactions (superconducting properties, line widths, etc.)
  • Linear-response (phonon modes, dispersion, interatomic force constants, vibrational DOS, etc.)
  • Magnetic (magnetics, magnetization, magnons, etc.)
  • Microscopy, electron (S/TEM, 4D-STEM, SAED, etc.)
  • Microscopy, scanning probe (STM, AFM, etc.)
  • NMR (chemical shifts)
  • Optical (electronic excitation spectra, low-loss EELS, etc.)
  • Spectroscopy, core-level (XAS, XES, core-loss EELS, XPS, etc.)
  • Spectroscopy, vibrational (Raman, Infrared spectroscopy, etc.)
  • Transport (electronic conductivity, thermal conductivity, etc.)
  • X-ray scattering (diffraction, reflectivity, pair-distribution function, etc.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

derived-property*

Details of a quantity related to material behavior computed based on a computational materials science (CMS) calculation covered by the MatCore standard.

Required Repeatable yes yes type*

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

calculation-method*

Details regarding an approach used to obtain the derived property. Multiple approaches may be involved in the computation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

A parameter associated with the specified calculation method.

docs.title: Annex I — Identifier Schemes
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

(Normative)

docs.title: I.1 Purpose
docs.text: This annex defines the identifier schemes whose values a MatCore validator checks. An identifier property has two subproperties: value, the identifier itself, and scheme, the name of the scheme it belongs to. The scheme names the rule that value follows.

docs.title: I.2 Rules
docs.text:
1. When scheme is a scheme listed in Table I.1, value SHALL be written in that scheme's form, SHALL match its pattern in full, and SHALL pass its check digit if the scheme has one.
  2. A scheme not listed in Table I.1 is permitted. Its value is not checked, and a validator reports it as user-specified.
  3. Scheme names are written exactly as in Table I.1.
  4. Check digits:
    • ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2: computed over the 16 characters of the identifier, hyphens removed; the last character is the check character, where X stands for 10.
    • ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 97-10 (ROR): the last two digits of a ROR ID are the MOD 97-10 check of the number encoded, in Crockford base 32, by the six characters after the leading 0.
  5. A scheme is added, or its rule changed, only by revision of this annex. Every field of an entry is traced to the scheme's own documentation, named in the Source column.

docs.title: Annex U — MatCore Unit Table
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

(Normative)

Amended 2026-10-31: Rule 4 extended from generic parameters to any subproperty whose Kind the schema declares as any (decision record 0001).

docs.title: U.1 Purpose
docs.text:
This annex defines the closed set of unit symbols that MAY appear as the value of a unit subproperty in a MatCore metadata instance, the kind of each symbol, and its conversion to coherent SI. It also defines the kind names used in the Kind field of the schema and their mapping to the QUDT ontology.

A validator checks that (a) the symbol is in Table U.4 and (b) its kind matches the kind declared for the property in the schema. No unit parsing is required.

docs.title: U.2 Rules
docs.text:
1. Symbols are case-sensitive ASCII strings. eV and ev are not the same symbol.
  2. Compound symbols use / for division and ^ for integer exponents, exactly as written in Table U.4. Symbols not listed (e.g. eV/A, Å, angstrom**3) are non-conformant.
  3. The reserved symbol dimensionless is used for quantities of dimension one (ratios, counts, fractional coordinates). It SHALL NOT be used for plane angles (use rad or degree) or for amount of substance (use mol).
  4. A unit subproperty of a generic parameter or of any other subproperty whose Kind the schema declares as any MAY, if and only if no symbol in Table U.4 applies, contain a string of the form x-gnu:<expression>, where <expression> is a unit expression valid in GNU Units 2.23 with definitions.units version 3.19 (February 2024). Such values are accepted with a validation warning and are not guaranteed to be machine-convertible. Later versions of definitions.units are not implied; a change of the pinned version is a revision of this annex.
  5. Conversion factors marked exact follow from the SI definitions. Factors marked CODATA 2022 are the 2022 CODATA recommended values published by NIST. The factors in Table U.4 are normative for MatCore and take precedence over the values embedded in any external vocabulary (see Note 5). A revision to a later CODATA release is a revision of this annex.
  6. This annex is versioned with the standard. Instance files SHALL use symbols from the annex version matching their declared MatCore version. Symbols are only ever added; a symbol, once published, is never removed or redefined.
  7. Compatibility between a unit and a kind is decided by the SI dimension vector in Table U.3, not by QUDT's own hasQuantityKind links (see Note 4).
  8. Energy and MolarEnergy are distinct kinds and are not interchangeable. A property declared with Kind Energy SHALL NOT carry a MolarEnergy unit, and vice versa (see Note 1).

docs.title: U.3 Kinds

They are the customary energy units of classical force fields, and properties in the MD section that are conventionally reported per mole are declared with Kind MolarEnergy. Conversion between Energy and MolarEnergy is a division or multiplication by the Avogadro constant (6.022 140 76 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, exact) and is a task for tooling, not for a unit value.

Note 2 (2π convention). InverseLength symbols do not encode whether a factor 2π is included. Properties for which this matters (e.g. k-point-spacing) carry a separate required convention subproperty.

Note 3 (mole vs. dimensionless). Following OPTIMADE, dimensionless SHALL NOT be used for amounts of substance or plane angles.

Note 4 (QUDT quantity-kind links are not a validation basis). QUDT attaches its own quantity kinds to units, and these are often narrower or differently named than MatCore's: PER-SEC is linked to Frequency and DecayConstant (not InverseTime); PER-M3 to InverseVolume (not NumberDensity); W-PER-M2 to PowerPerArea (not HeatFluxDensity); GigaPA, KiloBAR and BAR to ForcePerArea (not Pressure); EV-PER-ANGSTROM to TotalLinearStoppingPower (not Force). In every case the dimension vector agrees with the MatCore kind, so compatibility is validated by dimension vector (Rule 7), and the QUDT unit IRI serves only as a stable identifier.

Note 5 (stale constants in reference vocabularies). QUDT's own conversion multipliers for E_h (4.359 743 94 × 10⁻¹⁸ J) and AMU (1.660 538 782 83 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) are CODATA 2006 values, and GNU Units 2.23 uses CODATA 2018 values (hartree 4.359 744 722 2071 × 10⁻¹⁸ J, bohrradius 5.291 772 109 02 × 10⁻¹¹ m, amu 1.660 539 066 6 × 10⁻²⁷ kg). The factors in Table U.4 are therefore normative in MatCore (Rule 5) and take precedence over the values embedded in either reference vocabulary.

Note 6 (GNU spelling of bohr). GNU Units does not define bohr; the GNU name is bohrradius. The MatCore symbol remains bohr; the mapping is given in the GNU column.

Note 7 (units absent from QUDT). Ry, bohr, meV, nm^3, 1/ps, 1/bohr, bohr^3, K/angstrom, eV/angstrom^3, hartree/bohr, 1/angstrom^3, V/angstrom and mu_B have no unit IRI in QUDT Units v3.3.0. For these, the MatCore symbol is the identifier and the quantity-kind IRI in Table U.3 supplies the semantic anchor. QUDT accepts contributions through its public repository, and IRIs will be added to this table if and when they are published.

docs.title: 2.3 Particle Interaction Model (PIM) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

The metadata for particle interaction models (MatCore-PIM) is tabulated below. A particle interaction model gives the energy and forces of a system of particles as an explicit function of the particles' coordinates, without solving for a wavefunction or an electron density, e.g. an interatomic potential, a machine-learned interatomic potential, a bonded force field, a coarse-grained model or the electron force field. These properties describe a computation whose method is PIM, the evaluation of energies and forces used by another computation, e.g. molecular dynamics. The properties are given in settings blocks, each naming the PIM computations it describes. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

settings*

Settings shared by the computations named in it.

Required Repeatable yes yes computation-label*

The label of a computation these settings apply to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable — theory-level*

How the functional form of the model was obtained.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Physics-based, Machine-learned. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Physics-based" – A functional form built from a physical model of the interactions, with parameters fitted to data, e.g. EAM, Tersoff, a bonded force field or the electron force field. "Machine-learned" – A machine learning model trained to take particle positions as input, e.g. GAP or MACE.

model-type*

The kind of potential used to compute the particle interactions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Lennard-Jones, EAM, MACE.

Note: Give the functional form. The specific parameterization, e.g. an OpenKIM model, NIST IPR record, or a published potential file, is identified in the computation's software (role Interaction model).

particle-style*

The nature of the discrete entities whose interactions the model describes.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Atom, Radical, United atom, Bead, Coarse grained, Mesoscale, Classical electron, Nucleus. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Atom" – Each particle represents an individual atom. "Radical" – Each particle represents a free radical. "United atom" – Each particle represents a fixed grouping of atoms. "Bead" – Each particle represents a user-tuneable group of atoms. "Coarse grained" – Each particle represents a higher scale particle obtained by scaling up the atomic representation. "Mesoscale" – Granular particles used to simulate microstructure at the mesoscopic scale. "Classical electron" – Antisymmetrized wave packet representation of valence electrons. "Nucleus" – A nucleus or an ion core as a point charge, with its electrons represented by other particles, e.g. in the electron force field. Give one entry for each kind of particle the model has, e.g. Nucleus and Classical electron for the electron force field.

bonding-type*

Specifies whether the bonds between particles are immutable or can be broken.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Reactive, Bonded fixed, Bonded mutable. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Reactive" – A model without a predetermined bonding topology in which bonds are formed or broken on-the-fly based on the particle environment. "Bonded fixed" – Bonds defined a priori and cannot be broken during a simulation. "Bonded mutable" – Bonds defined a priori but can be broken and/or formed during a simulation.

charge-interactions

The model used to describe the interactions between charged particles.

Required Repeatable no yes charge-origin*

Nature of the particle charges.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Semi empirical, Quantum, Electronic population, Electronegativity, Tabulated. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Semi empirical" – Charges obtained from semi-empirical quantum calculations. "Quantum" – Charges obtained from quantum calculations. "Electronic population" – Charges obtained from electronic population analysis, e.g. Mulliken. "Electronegativity" – Charges obtained from electronegativity differences between atoms. "Tabulated" – Charges obtained from an external source.

charge-style*

The nature of the charges associated with the particles, such as total or effective charges.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Coulomb full, Coulomb screened. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Coulomb full" – The particle charge accounting for all electrons. "Coulomb screened" – Effective charge due to screening or shielding by other electrons (e.g. Slater).

charge-variability*

Attribute specifying the method for dynamically varying the local electric charge associated with discrete entities.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Fixed, QEq, EEM, iEL/SCF, FlucQ, Drude. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Fixed" – Charges cannot change during a simulation. "QEq" – Charge equilibration method. "EEM" – Electronegativity Equalization Method. "iEL/SCF" – Extended Lagrangian/self-consistent field scheme. "FlucQ" – Fluctuating charge potential. "Drude" – Drude method.

long-range-electrostatics

Method used to compute long-range electrostatic interactions.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: None, Direct, Ewald, PME, PPPM, Reaction. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "None" – No electrostatic calculation performed. "Direct" – All Coulomb interactions computed directly. "Ewald" – Ewald summation. "PME" – Particle mesh Ewald. "PPPM" – Particle particle particle mesh. "Reaction" – Reaction field.

electric-dipole

Attribute specifying the type of interaction associated with the local electric dipoles associated with particles.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Stockmayer, Screened, Long range. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Stockmayer" – Stockmayer potential. "Screened" – Screened dipoles. "Long range" – Long-range dipoles.

electric-dipole-variability

Attribute specifying the method for dynamically varying the local electric dipoles associated with discrete entities.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Induced, Isotropic, Anisotropic. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Induced" – Induced point dipoles. "Isotropic" – Isotropic polarizability. "Anisotropic" – Anisotropic polarizability.

magnetic-interactions

The model used to describe the interactions between magnetic spins.

Required Repeatable no yes spin-style*

The nature of the magnetic spins associated with the particles.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no string [] inapplicable —

Recommended: Classical spin, Coupled spin lattice. Other values are allowed.

Clarifications: "Classical spin" – Spins modeled as classical vectors evolved via the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert (LLG) equation defined by a spin Hamiltonian. "Coupled spin lattice" – Classical spins whose spin Hamiltonian depends on the particle positions, so that the spins and the particles evolve together. Magnetism obtained from the electrons, e.g. by spin-polarized DFT or tight binding, is a computation of its own (method DFT or TB), which the computation that uses it names as an input with the role Interaction model.

magnetic-dipole

Attribute specifying the type of interaction (spin Hamiltonian) between the magnetic dipoles associated with particles.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no string [] inapplicable —

Examples: Heisenberg, Multi-spin, Zeeman.

Note: The strength of an applied field is the condition magnetic-field in minimal conditions; a Zeeman term names its coupling to the spins.

docs.title: 2.4 Particle Simulation (PS) Metadata
docs.text:
Version 0.6.0

The metadata for particle simulations (MatCore-PS) is tabulated below. A particle simulation moves or samples a system of particles using the energies and forces supplied by an interaction model, a particle interaction model or, as in ab initio molecular dynamics, an electronic structure computation. This category includes molecular dynamics (MD), molecular statics (MS), Monte Carlo (MC) and their coarse-grained forms: energy and free energy minimization, equilibrium and nonequilibrium MD, accelerated dynamics, enhanced sampling, saddle-point searches and related approaches. The properties are given in settings blocks, each naming the PS computations it describes. (Note: This standard inherits the metadata in the minimal MatCore standard, adding the properties below.)

* required appears at most once repeatable

settings*

Settings shared by the computations named in it.

Required Repeatable yes yes computation-label*

The label of a computation these settings apply to.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes yes string [] inapplicable — algorithm

The computational method used to perform the computation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values based on the specified calculation type:: For "Minimization": "Simplex" "Damped dynamics" "FIRE" "Steepest descent" "Conjugate gradients" "BFGS" "Simulated annealing" "SGLD" – Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "Equilibrium dynamics" or "nonequilibrium-dynamics": "Leap frog" "Runge-Kutta" "Velocity Verlet" "Verlet" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "Free energy": "Harmonic" "Metadynamics" "PMF" – Potential of Mean Force "Thermodynamic integration" "Umbrella sampling" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

computation-parameter

A fixed variable associated with the specified computation algorithm.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The designation of the parameter associated with the specified computation algorithm.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the name of the computation parameter.

value*

The data associated with the computation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: An integer, real, boolean, or string containing the computation parameter value.

unit*

A standardized string or identifier that defines the dimension or measurement system of the associated value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the units of the value in the GNU unit convention (or the text "dimensionless").

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the computation parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string explaining the computation parameter (e.g. "The convergence tolerance for energy minimization", "The simulation time for the dynamical simulation").

initialization

Information on the conditions set at the start of the simulation.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing a description of the simulation initial conditions (such as the nature and source of an initial structure, initialization of velocities or spins, etc.).

thermodynamic-constraint

Macroscopic physical restriction imposed on the simulation, such as a statistical mechanics ensemble.

Required Repeatable no yes system*

The collection of particles to which the constraint is applied.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String describing the constrained system (e.g. entire system, or a subset of atoms that are constrained.)

type*

The nature of the imposed thermodynamic constraint.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values: "NVE" – Microcanonical "NVT" – Canonical "μVT" – Grand canonical "NPT" – Isothermal-isobaric "NσT" – Isothermal-isostress "μPT" – Grand isothermal-isobaric "μσT" – Grand isothermal-isostress "NPH" – Isoenthalpic-isobaric "NσH" – Isoenthalpic-isostress Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

method

The name of the approach used to impose the constraint.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: String containing one of the following values based on the specified constraint:: For "NVT": "Andersen" "Berendsen" "CSVR" Langevin "Nosé-Hoover" "Nosé-Hoover chain" "Velocity rescaling" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "μVT": "GCMC" – Grand Canonical Monte Carlo Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "NPT": "Andersen" "Berendsen" "CauchyStat" "Nosé-Hoover style" "Parrinello-Rahman" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "NσT": "CauchyStat" "Parrinello-Rahman" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "μPT": User-specified value. For "μσT": User-specified value. For "NPH": "Nosé-Hoover style" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply. For "NσH": User-specified value. Otherwise: User-specified value.

description

Explanatory text about the constraint and method used to impose it.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the constraint description.

td-parameter

A fixed variable associated with the specified thermodynamic constraint.

Required Repeatable no yes name*

The designation of the parameter associated with the specified thermodynamic constraint.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: A string containing the name of the thermodynamic constraint parameter.

value*

The data associated with the thermodynamic constraint parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

Legacy: An integer, real, boolean, or string containing the thermodynamic constraint parameter value.

unit*

A standardized string or identifier that defines the dimension or measurement system of the associated value.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit yes no — — — —

description

An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the thermodynamic constraint parameter.

Required Repeatable Type Extent Kind Rec. unit no no — — — —
